description.value: Hidden Cove Lodge is an off-the-grid, ocean-front eco-lodge nestled in the rainforests of Northern Vancouver Island on Johnstone Strait, powered by wind, solar, and generator. The property offers ocean-side cottages and a dining room, and has held TripAdvisor's Certificate of Excellence since 2013. It sits in a remote and spectacular wildlife corridor — orca, humpback whales, and grizzly bears are common draws — making it a notable destination lodge for cyclists exploring the northern Island Highway corridor.

address.value: 1 Hidden Cove Road, Telegraph Cove, V0N 2R0

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website confirms the lodge is a real, operating eco-lodge at the OSM address with matching phone number. No cycling-specific content appears anywhere on the site — bike storage, staff procedures, laundry, Wi-Fi, or e-bike charging are all unmentioned. The lodge is explicitly off-the-grid (wind/solar/generator power), which makes Wi-Fi and e-bike charging plausible but unconfirmed; the job posting mentions a dining room and dinner service, suggesting on-site food, but no cyclist-specific meal arrangements are described.
concerns: Neither required criterion (secure bike storage, staff bike procedure) is mentioned anywhere on the website.
Lodge is off-the-grid (wind/solar/generator); Wi-Fi availability and e-bike charging capacity are unknown.
Seasonal operation: job posting states the lodge closes at end of September.
Contact page lists a separate mailing address (PO Box 258, Port McNeill, BC V0N 2R0) distinct from the physical address.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: The lodge is a legitimate, operating accommodation in a remote and cycle-relevant corridor, but the website contains no cycling-specific content — both required WWC criteria (secure bike storage and staff bike procedure) are entirely unconfirmed. Direct outreach is needed before this listing can be included.
enrichment_extras.notes: Lodge is in a very remote location approximately 12 minutes off Highway 19 on a gravel road. Nearest services (gas, groceries) appear to be Sayward (~1 hour south) or Port McNeill/Telegraph Cove (~20 minutes away per job posting). This context is worth capturing for cyclists planning a route.
